title: Freddie Jenkins the showman
summary: Jenkins was a showoff who clowned, as did Rex, and Tizol reflects that audiences applaud odd things.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: What do you remember about Freddie Jenkins?

Freddie Jenkins? Well, you know, he was a showman more than anything else. He played a little tambourine and then maracas and everything; he did everything; he was a showoff, boy. We didn't have no trouble with Freddie Jenkins. I used to get on him on account of for playing certain things that he wasn't supposed to be playing; just like Rex -- and clowning so much, with Duke, but I guess that's what he wanted anyhow.
The Duke kind of liked individualists, didn't he? I mean people who were different?
Well, he sold the band in many things. People, you know, people are crazy. The audience Sometimes they go for things that you would never think of.
People, even right now, there are a lot of people in the studio now and applaud performers that aren't worth five cents. Today they applaud for everything,
they laugh at jokes that don't mean anything. And the same thing at that time, too.
